20.en: "Supremacy is both the right and duty of Mankind. In the God-Emperor’s name, all else must fall."

38.en: The Imperium should be the most dominant force in the galaxy.

46.en: The Imperium can only survive if all opposing forces are eradicated.

54.en: All impurities within the Imperium must be exterminated.

76.en: Seek to purge any xenos or non-human entities that Humanity encounters without compromise. Promote the message of a dominant Humanity within the citizenry. Strive for purity within the Imperium by purging those guilty of witchcraft, heresy, and mutation.

82.en: Monodominants are ruthless Puritans who seek to perfect the Imperium and ensure the survival and dominance of Mankind by obliterating non-humans of all kinds, including daemons, mutants, and xenos in all their horrifying forms. Theirs is a militant stance, and they are notorious for ordering

86.en: in situations where other Inquisitors might seek another solution. They also keenly watch their Inquisitor brethren, searching for even the slightest signs of heresy. They do not hesitate to condemn their peers as heretics and take on the role of their executioner if necessary

90.en: They proudly trace the origins of their philosophy back to Inquisitor Goldo’s Monodomination, inscribed in the third century of the 33rd millennium. However, Inquisitor Jeriminus established the philosophy hundreds of years later when he swore to turn Goldo’s idealist vision into a reality. For the Monodominants, the Macharian Crusades stopped too soon. They would have preferred the fleets press on into the dark, annihilating all that is inhuman in their path, but Lord Macharius decided otherwise. Now, they work across the sector to purge any trace of heresy or taint.

94.en: Monodominants are seldom as secretive as other Inquisitors, using their reputation and the fear it inspires to encourage citizens to reveal mutants, xenos, and psykers wherever they go. While their cause is in line with the Inquisition’s, their methods are often more destructive than their brethren’s, and their tendency to turn on their own at the slightest suspicion of heresy makes them dangerous to work with.

110.en: Monodominants must be uncompromising in their views and actions. They will never consider allying with xenos, daemonic, or heretical forces. They will prescribe death to anyone in their presence who falters from their stance.

118.en: Many revere Humanity and its accomplishments, citing Humanity’s victories and most outstanding achievements as reasoning for their beliefs, as much as removing opposition as a necessity for survival.

126.en: They are less interested in subterfuge than their brethren in the Holy Orders. Monodominants often work out in the open, lean on their authority, act as militant leaders, and wield their terrifying presence openly as a weapon.

140.en: Informants report that the leaders of several voidports around Kharmin have been trading with xenos entities for additional supplies. Investigate these claims, purge those responsible and install new leadership at the voidports. But act with care; you must use the opportunity to set a trap for the xenos and destroy them.

148.en: Local cults on Pathway have mistaken a new mutation spreading throughout the populace as the God-Emperor’s blessing — improving people’s strength and overall size; some claim to be ‘angels’. Travel to Pathway, seek the source of this mutation, and purge all those affected. Reaffirm the people’s beliefs and get them to turn on these foul mutants.
